scope: Exploratory development-only diagnosis; candidate models refitted inside held-out related-group folds, not an independent evaluation of deployed artifacts
extraction_check: 654 original development rows and 26,814 feature/target cells reproduced from source reports with no mismatches at rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-10
fit_check: Both bundled ridge models reproduced within 1e-8 Gb prediction tolerance; no corrupted-artifact or unit-conversion explanation found in these checks
grouping: 121 connected components of original sample labels and flowcell IDs; five outer folds with zero sample-label or flowcell overlap

findings.finding: Raw-yield ridge can produce physically implausible predictions
findings.evidence: In-sample negative raw MinION predictions: 35/176 at 30 min and 46/181 at 60 min. Deployed predictor clips to zero, not to already observed passed yield. No development final yield was lower than observed checkpoint passed yield.

findings.finding: Device pooling and target scale contribute to early MinION error
findings.evidence: Controlled device-specific and log1p-target ablations reduce MinION validation MAE relative to the original mixed-device raw-Gb ridge recipe. This supports a formulation issue, not a proven unique cause of each recent error.

findings.finding: Early mixed-device target scales differ sharply
findings.evidence: PromethION contributes 96.8% and 99.1% of squared target magnitude at 30/60 min despite only 22/198 and 32/213 observations. These are target-magnitude shares, not fitted-loss shares.

Original outer folds grouped sample labels but allowed reused flowcells across folds. RidgeCV internal tuning followed preprocessing and was not explicitly grouped. The diagnostic retains that recipe to isolate effects; final replacement tuning must be redesigned.

MinION-only extra trees has lowest overall candidate MAE here, but beats extrapolation on only 85/165 and 82/167 matched runs. On the 26 three-hour runs, extrapolation has lower 60-minute MAE (0.0685 Gb versus 0.1399 Gb for trees).

recommendation: Develop a reproducible MinION-specific replacement in a separate development phase. Start with the tested tree and log-target ridge candidates plus simple extrapolation; select and tune using related-group folds with preprocessing inside tuning splits. Address the observed-yield lower bound and recalibrate intervals for the final frozen predictor. Keep existing deployed artifacts until replacement qualification and independent evaluation are complete.
limits: These are already-used development data and one fixed outer split; not confirmatory evidence or calibrated uncertainty for new candidates.
Changing the candidate based on these results is development. Do not rebrand S1-S30 outcomes as untouched future validation.
No live feature-parity or instrument-timing guarantee follows from successful historical extraction reproduction.
Short-run workflows still favor simple extrapolation in important subsets; retain it as a comparator.
